title: Where does one point four sit on a number line?
description: A number line runs from 1 to 2. The gap is cut into ten equal parts to place 1.4, and then the gap from 1 to 1.1 is cut into ten again to name its divisions. Keeko doubts that a gap between two whole numbers can hold any divisions at all.
teaching_notes: One idea: a gap between two numbers is cut into ten equal parts, and a part can be cut into ten again. Watch for students who count the marks instead of the parts.

source: Locate 1.4 on the number line. Then name all the divisions b
video_script.why: The child knows tenths and hundredths as place values and now sees them as lengths on a number line.
video_script.substitution: Cut the gap into ten equal parts, count four parts from the left end, then cut the first tenth into ten again.
video_script.anchor: the number line from 1 to 2 in the book, with 1.4 to be placed on it
video_script.wrong_move: Says a gap between two whole numbers has no divisions inside it.
video_script.payoff_line: Each small part is one hundredth

final_answer.value: 1.4 is the 4th mark after 1; the divisions are 1.01 to 1.09
final_answer.spoken: one point four is the fourth mark after one; the divisions are one point zero one to one point zero nine

hold_back: 1.4 is the 4th mark after 1; the divisions are 1.01 to 1.09
maths_rules: gap from 1 to 2 is cut into 10 equal parts, each part is 0.1
gap from 1 to 1.1 is 0.1 long, cut into 10 equal parts, each part is 0.1 / 10 = 0.01
video_script.design: One number line from 1 to 2 stays all video. The first tenth is magnified once. One colour marks the fourth tenth, another marks the hundredths.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line from 1 to 2 with a question mark above the gap from 1 to 1.1

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The line runs from one to two. Where does one point four sit on it?
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Then look at the gap from one to one point one. What divisions lie inside that gap?

beats.on_screen: the number line stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the end of the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 1.4 = 1 unit and 4 tenths; a tenth is one of ten equal parts of one unit

marks.mean: the number 1.4 splits into 1 unit and 4 tenths
marks.tenth: one unit is cut into ten equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='mean'/>One point four means one unit and four tenths.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>A tenth is one of ten equal parts of one unit. Dividing a unit this way is how we measure more exactly.

beats.on_screen: Given: a number line from 1 to 2; the decimal 1.4

marks.given: the line and the decimal are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a number line from one to two, and the decimal one point four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the place of 1.4; the divisions between 1 and 1.1

marks.find2: the divisions between 1 and 1.1 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to place one point four on the line.
<bookmark mark='find2'/>We also name the divisions between one and one point one.

marks.cut: nine marks appear and the gap is in ten equal parts
marks.why: the tenths digit of 1.4 lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, cut the gap from one to two into ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='why'/>We do this because one point four has tenths.
The marks read one point one, one point two, one point three, and so on.

marks.count: four parts are counted from one and the fourth mark lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count four parts from one, because one point four is one unit and four tenths.
The fourth mark is one point four.

beats.on_screen: cut 1 to 1.1 into 10 equal parts; each part = 0.1 / 10 = 0.01

marks.zoom: the gap from one to one point one is magnified and cut into ten parts

narration: <bookmark mark='zoom'/>Step three, cut the gap from one to one point one into ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='why'/>We do this because we want the smaller divisions.
A tenth cut into ten gives a hundredth.
<bookmark mark='read'/>Step four, read the marks from one, adding a hundredth each time.
They are one point zero one, one point zero two,
<bookmark mark='rest'/>and so on up to one point zero nine.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1.4 is the 4th mark after 1; the divisions are 1.01 to 1.09
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each small part is one hundredth.
One point four is the fourth mark after one.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The divisions are one point zero one to one point zero nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: no divisions between 1 and 2; the bubble is crossed out and the ten parts of the gap glow

marks.fix: the bubble is crossed out and the ten parts glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are no divisions between one and two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But one point four is a number, and it sits between one and two. The gap must hold marks, and we cut it into ten equal parts.
